title: Independent quality review: staff questionnaire
respondents: All employees, including bank staff and managers below the Registered Manager; not agency workers or students
summary: The anonymous staff part of the yearly independent quality review: what staff know about safeguarding, capacity, complaints and speaking up; what they see about time at visits, continuity, information, care plans, protective equipment and learning; and how they rate our care. Results go to the reviewer. About 10 minutes.
purpose: The Governance and Quality Assurance Policy requires an independent quality review every 12 months by a reviewer with no other role here. This questionnaire is its anonymous staff part: staff tell someone outside the management line what they know, what they see and how they rate our care, across the five key questions. It tests the Registered Manager's quarterly self-assessment (SUR-CQC-003) alongside the reviewer's staff interviews and record sampling. Thirteen shared staff questions let the reviewer compare what staff tell an outsider with what they tell us in our own surveys; a gap is itself a finding. It is never a rehearsal of what to tell an inspector: nobody briefs staff on answers, the knowledge questions give no hints, and nobody asks afterwards what anyone said.

timing.when: Once a year during the independent quality review: open for 2 weeks from the second Monday of March, in place of the speaking up survey (SUR-STF-010) that year; the March pulse is skipped; never in September

introduction:
An independent reviewer, who does not work for {{organisation}}, is checking the quality of our service, and would like your view. It takes about 10 minutes, in paid working time. It is anonymous: we cannot see who answered, and managers see only combined results, through the reviewer's report. Taking part is your choice. Please think about the last 3 months.

This survey cannot be used to raise a concern, because we cannot see who answered. To raise a concern, speak to any manager or our Speaking Up Lead, or use our Whistleblowing (Speaking Up) Policy.

This survey is not for urgent concerns. If you are worried about your safety or someone else's, or need help now, phone the office or, out of hours, the On-call Manager (number in your staff handbook). In an emergency, call 999.
privacyNotice:
{{organisation}} uses your answers, through an independent reviewer, to check and improve the quality of our care. Our legal reason is our legitimate interest in running a good, safe service.

The survey is anonymous: we do not record your name, so your answers cannot be traced to you and we cannot reply. CareFlow records only which branch an answer came from. Please do not write names. Only the Nominated Individual and the independent reviewer see individual answers. A paper form goes sealed to the reviewer, who enters it. Reports show results only for groups of 5 or more people, and comments only for groups of 10 or more. If a comment describes someone at risk, we will act on it as far as we can.

We keep individual answers for 1 year after the survey closes, under our Records Management and Retention Policy. To ask about how we use information, contact the HR Manager or our Data Protection Officer. You can also complain to the Information Commission.
closingMessage: Thank you. Your answers go to the independent reviewer. For your reference: report abuse or neglect by phoning the office or the On-call Manager before you leave the visit; if someone may not be able to make a decision about their care, tell the office the same day; to help someone complain, give them our complaints leaflet or put them in touch with the office; and you can speak up to any manager, our Speaking Up Lead, CQC or Protect.

howToRun: The Nominated Individual runs it for the independent reviewer under the Governance and Quality Assurance Policy, in place of the speaking up survey (SUR-STF-010) that year: it carries that survey's speaking-up and incident target questions word for word. Use Send or schedule with everyone in your branches, repeating yearly from the second Monday of March, kept open 14 days for staff (its end date a few days later, for paper forms to reach the reviewer: see below); skip the March pulse; never in September. CareFlow records the branch of each anonymous answer, never the person. Leave out the Registered Manager (their view is the self-assessment), agency workers and students. CareFlow refuses an anonymous survey that would reach fewer than 5 people.

No coaching (Inspection Readiness and Working with Regulators Guideline): no team meeting, supervision or message before or during the survey discusses what to say, reminders say only that it is open and anonymous, and nobody asks anyone afterwards what they answered. The knowledge questions have no hints; the correct routes appear only in the closing message, after the answers are sent. The yearly briefing on speaking freely to CQC is held at a different time of year. Set one reminder after 1 week in Reminders and follow-up: on an anonymous survey CareFlow sends it to everyone who has not answered, with no personal link, and never to one person. It is done in paid working time; paper on request, sealed to the reviewer. In the Independent reviewers panel of the period being run (never the repeating survey itself), the Nominated Individual chooses "Add a reviewer" and gives the reviewer's name and email (never a staff email: CareFlow refuses it). This makes a CareFlow account with only the "Independent reviewer" role, which has no access of its own, and emails the reviewer an invitation to set their own password; the link lasts 72 hours, and it arrives only if the organisation's email is set up. Making the account and giving access need "Surveys" (act). CareFlow takes no answers once a survey has closed, so set this survey's end date late enough for the last paper forms to reach the reviewer (for example 3 working days after the 2 weeks). Then give that account access to this survey only, until that end date (never more than 90 days), with no people chosen: on an anonymous survey the reviewer records anonymous answers only. The reviewer signs in at the normal CareFlow login, sees only "Surveys to record", enters each paper form with Record response, channel Paper (the account can record Telephone, In person or Paper), and never sees results, counts or other answers. When the review ends, choose End access, then switch the account off (Settings, Users); it can be given access again next year.

Who may open individual answers: the Nominated Individual only, who reads comments each working day while the survey is open and passes them, and the results, to the reviewer, whose account records answers (Telephone, In person or Paper) but never shows results. This is set in Who can see the answers: individual responses and results are limited to the Nominated Individual, showing from 5 answers. Super Admin, Admin and the person who made the survey can always see both, so keep those roles to staff who may open them. The response count shows only to staff with results access, here the Nominated Individual.
actingOnResults: The reviewer analyses the results by key question for the review report: each shared question against its policy target (concern acted on and not treated worse at least 80%, a route outside the line manager at least 90%, safe to report incidents at least 90%) and against the same question in the latest staff survey (SUR-STF-001) and speaking up survey (SUR-STF-010). A gap of 10 percentage points or more is reported as a finding about trust in our own surveys. Positive means Strongly agree or Agree, Always or Usually, Yes, I am sure, or Very good or Good, leaving out Does not apply to me and Prefer not to say; for routes, count anyone choosing an option other than the first.

Never show a result for fewer than 5; flag 5 to 9; show the role group breakdown, branch results and comments only for 10 or more; never cross role group with branch; branch speaking-up figures under 3 are reported only at organisation level (Whistleblowing (Speaking Up) Policy). Managers see only combined results, through the review report. Any key question where staff results are clearly worse than the Registered Manager's self-assessment is flagged to the Nominated Individual for challenge.

The Nominated Individual receives the report; findings go into the service improvement plan within 5 working days, and the Directors receive it with the satisfaction survey results at the governance meeting held by mid-May. Keep individual answers for 1 year after the survey closes; the review report is a governance record (Records Management and Retention Policy).

alerts.when: Knowing how to report abuse or neglect, what to do about capacity, or how to help someone complain answered No (anonymous: counts only).
alerts.action: After the survey closes, the Nominated Individual asks the Registered Manager to plan refresher sessions for all staff on that topic within 4 weeks, never aimed at anyone. The survey is anonymous: act on the pattern, never try to identify who answered.

rule.task: Staff unsure of safeguarding, capacity or complaints (anonymous)

alerts.when: A comment suggesting abuse or neglect of a person we support.
alerts.action: The Nominated Individual passes it to the safeguarding lead the same working day (Safeguarding Concerns: Reporting, Referral and Enquiry Procedure). Nobody tries to identify the writer.
A speaking-up concern with the Nominated Individual as case owner, because it is anonymous (Compliments, Feedback and Involvement Procedure; Whistleblowing (Speaking Up) Policy).

alerts.when: A comment describing bullying or harassment.
alerts.action: The Nominated Individual logs it as an anonymous report (Bullying, Harassment and Sexual Harassment Policy).
